skill.name: flow-nexus-platform
skill.description: Manage Flow Nexus authentication, sandboxes, app deployment, payments, storage, real-time streams, and coding challenges through MCP workflows.
skill.summary: Flow Nexus platform guide for account operations, cloud sandboxes, deployment, billing, storage, and challenge workflows.
skill.author: Flow Nexus

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are false positives from Markdown fences and JavaScript template literals in SKILL.md. Confirmed static risks involve API keys and connection strings in remote Flow Nexus examples. Semantic review found sandbox execution, secret forwarding, tool-enabled deployment, and billing risks; no prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: Remote sandbox command and code execution
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before sandbox_execute, startup_script, run_commands, package installation, or git clone operations. Document isolation, logging, and rollback.

remediation.issue: Secret forwarding to remote sandboxes and deployments
remediation.suggestion: Replace credential examples with safer placeholders. State that live API keys, database URLs, and Anthropic keys require secret storage or redacted inputs.
Require confirmation that displays dollar amount, threshold, account, and expected charge before payment links or auto-refill changes.

remediation.issue: Broad tool access for the assistant example
remediation.suggestion: Default tool-enabled assistant examples to limited scope. Require separate approval before creating swarms, deploying code, or changing infrastructure.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Sandbox Code and Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents Flow Nexus calls that install packages, run commands, execute code strings, and run startup scripts. Startup scripts include package installs, git clone, and npm install. This is legitimate functionality, but it is high impact without explicit approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple examples explicitly invoke package installation, command execution, and arbitrary sandbox code execution. The risk is contextual rather than hidden malware, so confidence is high but not critical.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Credential Forwarding to Remote Workflows
semantic_findings.description: Examples ask users to pass environment variables, API keys, database URLs, and an Anthropic key into sandbox or deployment tools. Live values would be handled by Flow Nexus and could be exposed if the workflow is misused.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples explicitly include API keys, database URLs, and an Anthropic key parameter. The values are placeholders, but the documented workflow involves real secret transfer when used.

semantic_findings.title: Cost-Incurring Billing and Auto-Refill Operations
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents payment link creation and auto-refill configuration with dollar amounts. Agent execution without explicit confirmation could initiate purchases or recurring credit refills.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples clearly show payment link creation and auto-refill settings with monetary amounts. This is a business-logic risk if delegated to an autonomous agent.

semantic_findings.title: Tool-Enabled Assistant Can Deploy Code and Create Swarms
semantic_findings.description: The Seraphina assistant example enables tools and states that it can create swarms, orchestrate agents, and deploy code. This expands agent authority unless the user scopes and confirms tool actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited text directly enables tools and describes deployment and orchestration capability. It is legitimate functionality, but it creates autonomy risk in agent-mediated use.

content.value_statement: Flow Nexus users need one guide for account, sandbox, deployment, billing, and challenge operations. This skill organizes the MCP commands into practical workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides registration, login, authentication status checks, profile updates, and user statistics.
Documents sandbox creation, configuration, code execution, file upload, logs, status checks, and deletion.
Covers app store search, template deployment, app publishing, updates, analytics, and installed apps.
Explains credit balances, rUv history, payment links, auto-refill settings, and cost optimization.
Shows storage uploads, file listing, public URLs, deletion, real-time subscriptions, and execution streams.
Includes challenge browsing, submissions, completion records, leaderboards, achievements, system health, and audit logs.
limitations: Requires Flow Nexus MCP tools, a valid account, and permissions for the requested operation.
Can trigger deployments, sandbox execution, deletions, and billing actions if the agent is allowed to proceed.
Does not implement Flow Nexus services; it documents and organizes existing MCP tool calls.
Secrets and database URLs must be handled through approved secret workflows, not pasted casually into chat.

prompt_templates.title: Check Account Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Flow Nexus platform skill to verify my auth status, show my profile, and summarize my credit balance. Ask before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Sandbox
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Node.js Flow Nexus sandbox for an API project with safe placeholder environment variables. Install Express and dotenv, then show status and logs.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Find backend templates, deploy the Express starter I choose with variables I provide, then subscribe to execution updates and summarize generated files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Governed Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced platform operations with approval points
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a full Flow Nexus workflow for publishing, deploying, monitoring, and cost-controlling a template app. Include confirmation points before billing, deployment, and secret use.

output_examples.input: I need a Node API sandbox for testing a small backend service.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms account status, proposes a sandbox configuration, requests approval, creates the sandbox, and summarizes its status, identifier, and logs.

output_examples.input: Deploy a backend template and watch the build progress.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists matching templates, asks you to select one, confirms cost and variables, deploys it, and reports stream status and next actions.

output_examples.input: Review my Flow Nexus spending and suggest cleanup steps.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks balance, payment history, and auto-refill settings, then recommends sandbox cleanup or budget changes without making purchases.

best_practices: Confirm before any payment, deployment, deletion, auto-refill change, package install, or sandbox execution.
Use placeholders in prompts and provide secrets only through approved secret storage or secure platform inputs.
Clean up unused sandboxes and storage, then review audit logs after important workflows.
anti_patterns: Running unreviewed startup scripts or installing packages from repositories you do not trust.
Sharing real API keys, Anthropic keys, or database URLs directly in chat transcripts.
Enabling autonomous tool use for deployment, billing, or swarms without clear confirmation boundaries.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It organizes Flow Nexus MCP operations for accounts, sandboxes, deployments, billing, storage, streams, and coding challenges.

faq.question: Does it run code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents tool workflows, but execution depends on available MCP tools and user approval.

faq.question: Can it manage billing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers balances, payment links, payment history, and auto-refill settings. Confirm every purchase or billing change.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with secrets?
faq.answer: Use caution. Remote sandboxes and deployments may receive environment variables, so use approved secret handling and avoid chat exposure.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it publish apps to Flow Nexus?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes app store publishing and update workflows when your account has permission and the source is ready.
